results.evidence: BroadcastSummary shows a 'Move to draft' button calling `moveToDraft`; the logic deletes schedules then `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(... {status:'draft'})` and `saveBroadcastFinished(drafted)`, so isReadOnly (`status !== 'draft'`) becomes false and the schedule is deleted so it can't send.

Condition is only `broadcast?.status === 'active' && !batchJobsLoading && batchJobs.length === 0`. It never checks that a pending schedule exists, so an active broadcast with no batch jobs and no schedule would still show it; it also is not shown for a recurring broadcast that already ran, which does have a pending schedule.

Launch calls `await deleteSchedules(projectId, broadcastId)` (list then destroy all) before `hogFlowsSchedulesCreate` with a new schedule, or before the batch job for 'now', so no old schedule is reused or left behind.

`activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` occurs BEFORE `deleteSchedules` and the schedule creation. Interruption in between leaves it live with no schedule; the catch does attempt a revert to draft but the ordering is not delete-then-activate.

The only guards are active status, `!batchJobsLoading`, and `batchJobs.length === 0`. There is no check for more than one schedule, or for a workflow altered into an unsafe shape. (Only the run-history conditions are partly covered.)
The button's `onClick={moveToDraft}` dispatches immediately; no confirmation dialog or cancel option is present.
moveToDraft only deletes schedules and sets draft, showing a single success toast 'Broadcast moved to draft'. It never cancels started runs and has no warning or cancel-failure messaging.
The patch touches only frontend files; there is no scheduler change re-verifying status before creating a run.
deleteSchedules discards existing schedules, and the new schedule is built with only rrule, starts_at and timezone; no variables from the previous schedule are carried over.

result:
A live scheduled broadcast can now be moved back to draft, and launching now replaces any existing schedule. I didn't run type checks, lint or tests, and I didn't add a test.

The changes are frontend-only, in `products/workflows/frontend/Broadcasts/`:

- **Relaunch fix** (`broadcastWizardLogic.ts`): before creating the new schedule (or the send-now job), launch lists the broadcast's schedules and deletes them all. That includes one paused after an audience edit. The new schedule is created fresh and active, so a relaunched broadcast sends at the chosen time. I did this in the frontend rather than changing the backend, because the schedule POST endpoint is also used by other callers and I didn't want to change its behaviour.
- **Move to draft** (`broadcastWizardLogic.ts`): a new `moveToDraft` action deletes the broadcast's schedules so nothing fires during editing, then sets its status to draft. The scene then swaps from the read-only summary to the editable wizard. There is a `movingToDraft` loading flag and an error toast if it fails.
- **Move to draft button** (`BroadcastSummary.tsx`): "Move to draft" appears next to the status tag when the broadcast is active and has no batch jobs yet, meaning it is scheduled but hasn't started sending.

I hand-edited the `broadcastWizardLogic.ts` type block for the new action and value instead of regenerating it. If typegen produces a diff, keep its output.

A recurring broadcast that has already sent at least once has a batch job, so the button is hidden for it and it still has no way to stop or edit.
